props.title: Four Seasons Hotel Denver
props.lede: Four Seasons Hotel Denver is a 45-story tower a few blocks from the Denver Center for the Performing Arts, and its Grand Ballroom is one of the city’s favorite places for a wedding or a gala.

headingText.html: There’s a terrace by the pool on the third floor with views of the city, so you can have the cocktail hour outside and dinner in the ballroom.

props.title: Live music in each Four Seasons Hotel Denver event space
props.lede: Here’s the act we’d pick for each space. Press play to hear it over the photo.

spaces.name: Grand Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Grand Ballroom is about 5,200 sq ft, for banquets of up to 350 guests. It divides into two equal halves, and it has its own pre-function area.
spaces.why: A six-piece band playing 90s and 2000s R&B and hip-hop, for when you want everyone dancing.

spaces.name: Cottonwood Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Cottonwood Ballroom is the hotel’s junior ballroom, about 3,400 sq ft, and it divides into two.
spaces.why: He can start as a duo and grow to a full band over the evening.

spaces.name: Pool Terrace
spaces.facts: The Pool Terrace is an outdoor event space on the third floor with views of the city, for banquets of up to 200.
spaces.why: Flamenco and rumba on Spanish guitar, for a cocktail hour or a dinner.
spaces.alt: Cocktail tables in orange linens around the lit pool on the rooftop terrace, with the clock tower behind.

spaces.name: Private dining and smaller spaces
spaces.facts: The hotel has three private dining spaces and seven smaller meeting spaces, for rehearsal dinners, client dinners and breakouts.
spaces.why: Upright bass and guitar, at a volume nobody has to raise their voice over.
spaces.alt: A private dining table beside a grand piano and tall windows over the city.

props.title: Planning music at Four Seasons Hotel Denver

rows.text: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space. The Grand Ballroom also has a stage and a sound system of its own.
We plan the layout, load-in and load-out with the hotel’s events team, who sign off on them ahead of time.
The Pool Terrace is outdoors, so we’ll plan the music with an indoor backup if the weather turns.
There’s valet parking at the hotel.

props.html: Questions to ask the Four Seasons Hotel Denver events team

items.html: Which spaces have an end time for amplified music, and when is it?
Does the hotel’s AV team need to connect or run the band’s sound, and is there a fee for that?
Where do vendors load in, and when can the band set up?
Is there power near where the band will play?
What wording do you need on the certificate of insurance?

props.html: Forward this list to the events team, or send us the answers and we’ll plan around them.
Questions about music at Four Seasons Hotel Denver

items.q: Can we bring our own band to a wedding at Four Seasons Hotel Denver?
items.a: Hotels like Four Seasons Hotel Denver generally let you book your own entertainment, within their rules on insurance, load-in and sound. Your event manager can confirm them for your date, and we send a certificate of insurance with every booking.

items.q: Does the band need the hotel’s AV team?
items.a: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space. The hotel’s AV team can add anything beyond that, and we’ll work out the details with your event manager.

items.q: Can one act play the ceremony, the cocktail hour and the reception?
items.a: Yes. The same act can move with you from The Pool Terrace to The Grand Ballroom, and one booking covers all of it.

items.q: How much does live music add to a wedding at Four Seasons Hotel Denver?
items.a: It depends on the size of the act and how much of the day it covers. Our pricing page has what live music costs in the Colorado market, and we’ll send a quote for your date.
